subject: MAP: accelerated evaluation & hosting governance — decision window and closeflow
messages:
From: Lisa Moreno <lisa@healthspan.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Diaz <carlos@healthspan.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for MAP and hosting selection

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Leadership is aligned that we need a tight MAP (mutual action plan) to choose a hosting lane and sign off before our Q3 pilot. Key asks from our side:
- Clear evaluation criteria (latency, cost delta, data residency) across Hosted / Dedicated / Private
- A short timeline we can share with procurement and infra (ideal: decision in two weeks)
- Anything Redwood needs from HealthSpan (access windows, eval data sample)

We also need to understand what the lift looks like for Private (on-prem) — security signoff will want a checklist. Attaching a spreadsheet with our internal constraints. Can your team propose a decision window and a small MAP we can publish?

Best,
Lisa
Lisa Moreno
Head of Product Operations, HealthSpan
Attachments: healthspan_constraints.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Moreno <lisa@healthspan.com>
Cc: Carlos Diaz <carlos@healthspan.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for MAP and hosting selection

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear asks.

High-level proposal: a 10-business-day accelerated MAP that focuses decision on three lanes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) with the following milestones:
1) Day 0–2: Redwood provides an evaluation checklist and a 2k-token sample run for each lane (we'll need the sample data you mentioned).
2) Day 3–6: Joint eval runs (latency/cost profiling) + security questionnaire turn-around for Private.
3) Day 7–8: Internal review & trial summary (we'll deliver an objective scoring matrix).
4) Day 9–10: Final decision window + procurement kickoff (SOW/price banding).

I looped in Karthik and Marissa for technical and ops details. I added a stub MAP spreadsheet and a latency/SLA comparison PDF as attachments for your review.

Quick notes: Hosted gets you fastest time-to-value — we can stand up a sandbox within 24 hours; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and a reserved pool which matters for peak nightly processing; Private is feasible but will require 3–4 weeks for network/audit completion depending on your security controls. We'll put estimated cost deltas into the MAP.

Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment call Monday to lock the timeline?

Thanks,
Jonas
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: healthspan_map_v1.xlsx; latency-sla-comparison.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lisa Moreno <lisa@healthspan.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for MAP and hosting selection

Lisa — adding technical clarity so you can weigh tradeoffs when you score lanes.

Hosted (sandbox):
- Pros: <24h sandbox, zero infra for HealthSpan, Redwood-managed key ops.
- Cons: Logical multi-tenant; data egress and put costs apply. We can offer VPC peering on request.
- Typical latency: p95 generation 120–180ms depending on model selection and prompt length.

Dedicated (reserved pool):
- Pros: Dedicated GPU capacity, better burst performance, isolated tenant scheduling. Ideal if you have predictable nightly throughput.
- Cons: Committed monthly cost.
- Typical latency: p95 80–130ms with same model under reserved pool.

Private (VPC / on-prem installation):
- Pros: Full control, meets strict residency/compliance needs.
- Cons: Network prep, certs, and audit evidence needed; onboarding 3–6 weeks if on-prem.
- Typical latency: varies — often ~60–120ms internal network but depends on your infra.

For evaluation, Karthik requests: a representative sample of inference payloads (anonymized), peak concurrency estimate, and acceptable p95 latency target. We'll instrument runs and produce a side-by-side scoring sheet.

- Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Tentative MAP milestones:

- 5/19–5/21: Eval runs and perf/cost reports
- 5/22: Scoring review and final decision window
- 5/24: Procurement kickoff (if decision = Dedicated or Private)

Attachments included: MAP timeline (spreadsheet), Private-onboard-checklist.docx (stub).

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
